name: Uzzi
overview: Uzzi was a male Levite who served as an overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem. He is identified as the son of Bani, marking him as part of the priestly tribe entrusted with religious duties in the post-exilic community. His role as overseer highlights a leadership position among the Levites during the time recorded in Nehemiah.
namesAndTitles: The name Uzzi means 'YHWH is [my] strength,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that points to reliance on the Lord's power. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:22, was not given directly by God but carries a clear declaration of divine strength.
familyAndRelationships: Uzzi is explicitly noted as the son of Bani, establishing a direct familial link within the Levitical line. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide further family details for Uzzi.
scriptureSignificance: Uzzi's significance lies in his leadership among the Levites in Jerusalem during the post-exilic period, as recorded in Nehemiah. His role as overseer would have involved responsibilities in organizing and supervising the Levites' duties related to temple worship and community service. This position underscores the restoration and order of God's people following the exile, emphasizing faithful service to the Lord.
